title: Weyerhaeuser Announces Leadership and Organizational Changes
body_markdown:
- Cristin Aragon appointed Senior Vice President and Chief Human Resources Officer
- Justin Nikbakhsh appointed Senior Vice President, Technology and Procurement
- Denise Merle, Senior Vice President and Chief Administration Officer, to retire at the end of 2026


SEATTLE


, Nov. 16, 2026


/[PRNewswire](http://www.prnewswire.com/) / --[Weyerhaeuser Company](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4823886-1&h=3604863143&u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.weyerhaeuser.com%2F&a=Weyerhaeuser+Company) (NYSE: WY) today announced the appointment of Cristin Aragon as senior vice president and chief human resources officer, and Justin Nikbakhsh as senior vice president of technology and procurement, with both changes effective January 1, 2027. Aragon and Nikbakhsh will be taking over for Denise Merle, senior vice president and chief administration officer, who is retiring at the end of 2026 but will serve as a strategic advisor to support the leadership transition.


Aragon, who has served as vice president of compensation, benefits and shared services since 2024, will oversee Weyerhaeuser's human resources organization, which in addition to her current functions includes HR business partnership, labor relations, recruiting, talent management and people development. She will also oversee the company's enterprise marketing and communications organization. Nikbakhsh, who has served as vice president and chief procurement officer since 2024, will have responsibility for information technology and cybersecurity, procurement and innovation, as well as the company's Integration Excellence program.


"We are excited to welcome Cristin and Justin to our senior management team," said Devin Stockfish, president and chief executive officer. "We look forward to leveraging their leadership and expertise as we continue driving operational excellence, accelerating innovation and continually enhancing the environment and experience we create for all our employees."


"I also want to thank Denise for her remarkable tenure with Weyerhaeuser," Stockfish added. "From her first days in accounting more than 45 years ago through her distinguished career building and leading our human resources, technology and corporate affairs organizations, Denise has had an indelible impact on our company and culture. We wish her the very best in her well-deserved retirement and appreciate her support as a strategic advisor through the transition."


**ABOUT CRISTIN ARAGON**
Cristin Aragon joined Weyerhaeuser in 2018 and has nearly 20 years of experience in a variety of human resources and legal roles. She currently leads the company's compensation and employee benefits strategies and programs, as well as HR shared services, including payroll, workforce management and the employee service center. She previously served as the senior HR director for Weyerhaeuser's Lumber business, and as senior corporate employment counsel. Before joining Weyerhaeuser, Aragon was a partner at Yarmuth Wilsdon PLLC, a litigation law firm in Seattle, where her practice focused on employment advising and litigation, and complex civil litigation. She began her legal career in 2007 at the global law firm K&L Gates LLP in Seattle. Aragon earned a bachelor of arts in political science from Western Washington University and her J.D. from Seattle University School of Law.


**ABOUT JUSTIN NIKBAKHSH**
Justin Nikbakhsh joined Weyerhaeuser in 2013 and has more than 23 years of experience across financial operations, information technology and system controls, procurement, and audit and risk management. Prior to his current role as chief procurement officer, he served as the executive business leader of a major SAP implementation project and also as vice president of financial operations, overseeing the finance and enterprise planning organizations. He also previously served as vice president of Wood Products financial operations, vice president of enterprise risk management and chief compliance officer, and director of internal audit. Before joining the company, Nikbakhsh was director of internal control services and the Sarbanes-Oxley program at Univar, Inc., and he started his career in public accounting at KPMG. He earned a bachelor of arts in business administration and a master of accounting from Washington State University, where he focused on accounting information systems. He is a certified public accountant and serves as chair for Seattle University's Accounting Advisory Board.


**ABOUT WEYERHAEUSER**[Weyerhaeuser Company](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4823886-1&h=2753950371&u=https%3A%2F%2Fc212.net%2Fc%2Flink%2F%3Ft%3D0%26l%3Den%26o%3D4101815-1%26h%3D1174798293%26u%3Dhttps%253A%252F%252Fwww.weyerhaeuser.com%252F%26a%3DWeyerhaeuser%2BCompany&a=Weyerhaeuser+Company) , one of the world's largest private owners of[timberlands](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4823886-1&h=3937812391&u=https%3A%2F%2Fc212.net%2Fc%2Flink%2F%3Ft%3D0%26l%3Den%26o%3D4101815-1%26h%3D2212425965%26u%3Dhttps%253A%252F%252Fwww.weyerhaeuser.com%252Ftimberlands%252F%26a%3Dtimberlands&a=timberlands) , began operations in 1900 and today owns or controls more than 10 million acres of timberlands in the U.S., as well as additional public timberlands managed under long-term licenses in Canada. Weyerhaeuser has been a global leader in sustainability for more than a century and manages 100 percent of its timberlands on a fully[sustainable](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4823886-1&h=3436231204&u=https%3A%2F%2Fc212.net%2Fc%2Flink%2F%3Ft%3D0%26l%3Den%26o%3D4101815-1%26h%3D1359679029%26u%3Dhttps%253A%252F%252Fwww.weyerhaeuser.com%252Fsustainability%252F%26a%3Dsustainable&a=sustainable) basis in compliance with internationally recognized sustainable forestry standards. Weyerhaeuser is also one of the largest manufacturers of[wood products](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4823886-1&h=2446844424&u=https%3A%2F%2Fc212.net%2Fc%2Flink%2F%3Ft%3D0%26l%3Den%26o%3D4101815-1%26h%3D3365376169%26u%3Dhttps%253A%252F%252Fwww.weyerhaeuser.com%252Fwoodproducts%252F%26a%3Dwood%2Bproducts&a=wood+products) in North America and operates additional business lines around product distribution,[climate solutions](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4823886-1&h=857889703&u=https%3A%2F%2Fc212.net%2Fc%2Flink%2F%3Ft%3D0%26l%3Den%26o%3D4101815-1%26h%3D292249118%26u%3Dhttps%253A%252F%252Fwww.weyerhaeuser.com%252Fclimate-solutions%252F%26a%3Dclimate%2Bsolutions&a=climate+solutions) ,[real estate](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4823886-1&h=2013181569&u=https%3A%2F%2Fc212.net%2Fc%2Flink%2F%3Ft%3D0%26l%3Den%26o%3D4101815-1%26h%3D433984009%26u%3Dhttps%253A%252F%252Fwww.weyerhaeuser.com%252Fland%252Fcontact-us%252F%26a%3Dreal%2Bestate&a=real+estate) , energy and natural resources, among others. In 2025, the company generated $6.9 billion in net sales and employed approximately 9,500 people who serve customers worldwide. Operated as a real estate investment trust, Weyerhaeuser's common stock trades on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol WY.
